topic: Clinic Intake AI Safety Card: 7 Checks Before Automating Patient Questions
boundary: Educational operations guide only — not medical, legal, privacy, compliance, diagnosis, treatment, certification, savings, ranking, customer-result, approval, or guaranteed-performance advice.

checks.owner_question: Which intake questions are administrative only, such as location, hours, appointment type, documents, or callback preference?
checks.safe_action: Keep medical symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, urgency, and medication questions routed to humans.

checks.owner_question: When must the AI stop and send the person to staff or emergency guidance already approved by the clinic?
checks.safe_action: Write a visible handoff rule before connecting the intake tool to patients.

checks.owner_question: What personal or health details should not be typed into a public chat or unmanaged form?
checks.safe_action: Collect the minimum needed and avoid free-text medical history in low-control channels.

checks.owner_question: Has the clinic owner reviewed the exact phrases patients will see?
checks.safe_action: Use simple scripted wording and avoid advice, reassurance, diagnosis, or promise language.

checks.owner_question: Who reads escalated messages, missed calls, incomplete forms, and confused replies each business day?
checks.safe_action: Name a staff owner before increasing intake automation volume.

checks.owner_question: What happens for urgent symptoms, angry patients, minors, billing concerns, language gaps, or repeated messages?
checks.safe_action: Run a small internal test log and fix unsafe flows before public use.

checks.owner_question: Which questions repeated, which handoffs worked, and where did patients still need help?
checks.safe_action: Track themes, handoffs, unanswered items, and owner notes before expanding automation.

safe_scope: Uses administrative-scope boundaries, handoff rules, minimal collection, approved wording, response ownership, edge-case testing, and weekly owner evidence review; no patient data, credentials, medical advice, legal advice, privacy advice, compliance approval, guaranteed growth, or result claims.
